target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: triangular PATO_0001875 and ovate FLOPO:0991024)
reason: A compound of two outline shapes, like 'linear-lanceolate'; both values exist and the pair is written as a continuum, not a new term.
Tumescent fruits and peduncle bases are swollen and full; FLOPO turgid has exactly that meaning, and PATO swollen (PATO_0001851) is a transient abnormal enlargement, so it does not fit.

target: new: order of division (bifurcated PATO_0001784, repeated twice)
reason: Forked is bifurcated; 'twice' gives the number of successive branchings, an open pattern (order of division) in docs/annotation-context-patterns.md, not a separate quality.
'Without ribs' negates ribbed; a rib is a generic part (rejected as a bearer in the previous review), so the absence of the ribbed quality is the right reading.
A count of radiating arms or lobes of the fruit, like '5-nerved'; 'rayed' needs a row in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv for the counted part, which has no clear PO class.
A loment-like fruit is constricted between the seeds and breaks at joints into one-seeded segments, which matches FLOPO jointed; moniliform (FLOPO:0991168) would cover only the outline.
'Like a tortoise shell' means a vaulted calyx lip in one flora and a sculptured endocarp in the other; the word is a figurative comparison with no single quality behind it.
Unipinnatisect is once-pinnatisect, which is the plain pinnatisect class; bipinnatisect (FLOPO:0991284) is the twice-divided sibling.
Ash-coloured bark is grey; PATO has no finer ash-grey shade, and the colour is not worth a new term.
Describes how a moss alar region or acumen blends into the surrounding cells or lamina: a relation without its second term and a gradient, not a quality of the part.

target: 00-part-and-quality.md (vascular bundle PO_0005020 part of the bearer, green PATO_0000320)
reason: The colour belongs to the veins of the phyllary or petal, not to the organ; it is a part of a part with a colour, as 'veined' was mapped to vascular bundle.
Ligulate is strap-shaped (previous rule C189); 'long' only stresses the elongation, which is already part of the strap shape.
A double moss costa is two costae per leaf: a count of a PO part, not a quality.
The noun is not a quality; the statements ('loosely', 'tightly', 'evenly foliate') describe how leaves are spaced along the stem, which is a quality of the leaves towards each other.
The height of an endostome basal membrane is given relative to the endostome without naming it; a degree of an implicit comparison, like 'smaller'.
A radiculose moss stem bears rhizoids; 'sparsely' is a density qualifier kept in the record.

target: 00-part-and-quality.md (plant organ base FLOPO_0985024 of the bearer, increased width PATO_0000600) with 01-approximate-value.md for 'slightly'
reason: The widening belongs to the base of the filament or leaf ('widened' → increased width, rule C182); 'slightly' is a degree qualifier.
'Compact' is condensed (rule C188); 'very' is a degree qualifier.
'As long as the sepals': equality of length with another part, which pattern 10 covers.
A comparison of length of the wings or standard with the keel (PO_0025327); the second term is given, so pattern 09 applies.
'Few-leafleted' is an indefinite count, like 'few-flowered'.

target: new: position of a part on its whole (hilum PO_0020063 on the seed, between base and side)
reason: The word places the hilum on the seed, near the base and towards one side; pattern 18 covers a part's position among parts of its kind, not its place on a whole, and FLOPO basal is about arising from a stem.
French 'oppositifoliés' inflorescences arise opposite a leaf; this is leaf-opposed, not about leaflets (the English label is a mistranslation).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between saucer-shaped FLOPO:0991182 and cup-shaped PATO_0002227, the second approximate)
reason: A compound of two existing shape values, the second with 'sub-' as approximate; patelliform (dish-shaped) is saucer-shaped.
A comparison stated without its second term; with its term ('as long as the ovary') it is pattern 10, as for 'shorter' in the previous review.
French 'cannelé' stems and branches have longitudinal grooves: FLOPO sulcate, a child of PATO furrowed (to which 'fluted' was mapped).
An eight-sided outline or section is polygonal (five or more straight sides); a separate eight-sided class is not worth adding for 5 statements.
Same source word as 'opposite-foliolate': inflorescences opposite a leaf.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: spreading PATO_0104356 and decumbent PATO_0002343)
reason: Stigmatic branches that radiate outwards and lie down are a compound of two orientation values; FLOPO radiate (FLOPO:0991194) is the capitulum sense and does not apply.
A 'rich' inflorescence is many-flowered ('plus de 10 fleurs'): an indefinite count of flowers.
